subject: math
title: Area of Triangles, Parallelograms, Trapezoids and Polygons
seo_title: Grade 6 Area of Polygons Worksheets: Triangles, Parallelograms, Trapezoids and Composite Figures
standard_text: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 area of polygons worksheets: area of right triangles and other triangles (A = ½bh), parallelograms (A = bh), trapezoids, and composite figures split into rectangles and triangles, plus real-world word problems. 100 practice questions with answer key.
key_big: Triangle: A = ½ × b × h. Parallelogram: A = b × h. Trapezoid: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h.
key_sub: The height always meets the base at a right angle; a slanted side is not the height. For other polygons, split the shape into rectangles and triangles and add, or subtract the missing piece. Area is in square units (ft², m²).
body_html:
The big idea: rearrange into rectangles

You already know the area of a rectangle: base × height. Every formula in this unit comes from cutting a shape apart or putting two copies together to make a rectangle. The height is always measured straight across at a right angle to the base. It is shown as a dashed line with a small square at the corner.

Parallelograms: A = b × h

Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. The parallelogram becomes a rectangle with the same base and the same height.

Triangles: A = 12 × b × h

Two copies of any triangle make a parallelogram, so a triangle is half of it. For a right triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height.

In an obtuse triangle the height can fall outside the triangle. Extend the base with a dashed line and measure the height to that line.

Trapezoids: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h

Two copies of a trapezoid, one turned upside down, make a parallelogram with base b1 + b2. The trapezoid is half of it.

Example

A trapezoid has parallel sides of 9 m and 5 m. They are 4 m apart. Find the area.

Add the bases: 9 + 5 = 14. Multiply by the height: 14 × 4 = 56. Take half: 56 ÷ 2 = 28.

Answer: 28 m²

Composite figures: split or subtract

Split the figure into rectangles and triangles that do not overlap, then add their areas. Or start with a big rectangle and subtract the piece that is missing.

Subtract a piece

A 10 m by 8 m rectangle has a triangle cut out. The triangle has a base of 8 m and a height of 3 m. Find the area left.

Rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80. Triangle: 12 × 8 × 3 = 12. Subtract: 80 − 12 = 68.

Answer: 68 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Triangle: 14 × 12 = 168Take half: 12 × 14 × 12 = 84
Using the slanted 13 m side as the heightUse the dashed height at a right angle to the base
Trapezoid: (16 + 6) × 12 = 264Take half: 12 × 22 × 12 = 132
Adding the side lengths (that is the perimeter)Area multiplies base and height
Counting a corner twice in an L-shapeSplit into pieces that do not overlap
Writing 84 ft for an areaArea is in square units: 84 ft²

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
faq.a: A = ½ × base × height. The height must meet the base at a right angle, so it is not usually a side of the triangle (except in a right triangle).

faq.q: Why do you divide by 2 to find the area of a triangle?
faq.a: Two copies of the same triangle fit together to make a parallelogram (or a rectangle for a right triangle). The triangle is half of that shape, so its area is half of base × height.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a trapezoid?
faq.a: Add the two parallel sides, multiply by the height, and take half: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. For bases of 16 in and 6 in and a height of 12 in, A = ½ × 22 × 12 = 132 in².

faq.q: How do you find the area of an irregular polygon in Grade 6?
faq.a: Split it into rectangles and triangles that do not overlap, find each area, and add them. You can also start with a larger rectangle and subtract the missing pieces (6.G.A.1).

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 7 × 5 = 35 m². The shaded triangle is half of it: 35 ÷ 2 = 17.5 m².

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 14 × 6 = 12 × 84 = 42 m².

items.q: Which expression gives the area of this right triangle?
items.e: Use the two sides that make the right angle: they are the base and the height. 12 × 3 × 4 = 6 in². 3 × 4 forgets the 12, and 5 in is the slanted side.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?

items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 5 × 12 = 12 × 60 = 30 cm². The 13 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A right triangle has sides that are 8 m, 6 m and 10 m long. What is its area?
items.e: The longest side (10 m) is across from the right angle, so it is slanted. Use the two shorter sides: A = 12 × 8 × 6 = 12 × 48 = 24 m².

items.q: The two sides that meet at the right angle of a right triangle are 9 cm and 14 cm long. What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: A = 12 × 9 × 14 = 12 × 126 = 63 cm². Do not forget the 12: a triangle is half of a rectangle.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 15 × 8 = 12 × 120 = 60 in². The 17 in side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.e: 12 × 5 × ? = 30, so 5 × ? = 30 × 2 = 60. 60 ÷ 5 = 12 ft. Check: 12 × 5 × 12 = 12 × 60 = 30.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a height of 11.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 11.5 = 161 cm². No 12 here: a parallelogram is a rectangle with a slanted end moved.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 7 × 3 = 21 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 m side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 7 by 3.)

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (20 + 10) × 12 = 12 × 30 × 12 = 180 in². The 13 in side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (26 + 8) × 12 = 12 × 34 × 12 = 204 cm². The 15 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 m side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 7 by 4.)

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (15 + 5) × 12 = 12 × 20 × 12 = 120 m². The 13 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 16 × 15 = 240 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 17 cm side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 16 by 15.)

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (17 + 5) × 8 = 12 × 22 × 8 = 88 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 8.5 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 8.5 × 6 = 51 ft². No 12 here: a parallelogram is a rectangle with a slanted end moved.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: Add the two parallel sides, multiply by the height (the dashed line), and take half: 12 × (14 + 8) × 4 = 12 × 22 × 4 = 44 m².

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 18 × 8 = 144 ft². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 ft side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 18 by 8.)

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 12 m and 7.5 m. The distance between them (the height) is 4 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × (12 + 7.5) × 4 = 12 × 19.5 × 4 = 39 m².

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: Add the two parallel sides, multiply by the height (the dashed line), and take half: 12 × (16 + 6) × 12 = 12 × 22 × 12 = 132 ft².

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (9 + 7) × 9 = 12 × 16 × 9 = 72 ft².

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 18 × 16 = 288 in². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 20 in side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 18 by 16.)

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (11 + 8) × 8 = 12 × 19 × 8 = 76 in².

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 7 cm and 13 cm and an area of 60 cm². What is its height?
items.e: 12 × (7 + 13) × h = 60, so 12 × 20 × h = 60, which is 10 × h = 60. h = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 cm. Check: 12 × 20 × 6 = 60.

sets.title: Composite figures: split into rectangles and triangles

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 9 = 54 and 9 × 5 = 45. Add: 54 + 45 = 99 cm². Use each part of the figure once: 6 × 9 + 15 × 5 = 129 counts the 6 × 5 corner twice.

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (gray dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 9 × 8 = 72 m². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 3 × 4 = 12 × 12 = 6 m². Subtract: 72 − 6 = 66 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 9 = 54 m². Triangle: 12 × 6 × 7 = 12 × 42 = 21 m². Add: 54 + 21 = 75 m².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 4 × 7 = 28 and 6 × 3 = 18. Add: 28 + 18 = 46 m². Use each part of the figure once: 4 × 7 + 10 × 3 = 58 counts the 4 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 13 × 4 = 52 cm². Triangle: its base is the 4 cm side and its height is 3 cm, so 12 × 4 × 3 = 12 × 12 = 6 cm². Add: 52 + 6 = 58 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle 11 × 7 = 77, minus the missing corner 5 × 4 = 20: 77 − 20 = 57 in². Or: split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 42 + 15 = 57 in².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². The triangle's base is 14 − 10 = 4 cm and its height is 4 cm: 12 × 4 × 4 = 12 × 16 = 8 cm². Add: 40 + 8 = 48 cm².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 8 = 96 in². Each triangle: base 8 in, height 5 in, so 12 × 8 × 5 = 12 × 40 = 20 in². Total: 96 + 20 + 20 = 136 in².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 10 = 90 in². Triangle: its base is the 10 in side and its height is 8 in, so 12 × 10 × 8 = 12 × 80 = 40 in². Add: 90 + 40 = 130 in².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 13 − 9 = 4 cm tall. Rectangle: 14 × 9 = 126 cm². Triangle: 12 × 14 × 4 = 12 × 56 = 28 cm². Add: 126 + 28 = 154 cm².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 14 × 5 = 70 in². Triangle: 12 × 14 × 4 = 12 × 56 = 28 in². Add: 70 + 28 = 98 in².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (gray dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 14 × 10 = 140 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 3 × 5 = 12 × 15 = 7.5 cm². Subtract: 140 − 7.5 = 132.5 cm².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 11 − 4 = 7 ft tall. Rectangle: 14 × 4 = 56 ft². Triangle: 12 × 14 × 7 = 12 × 98 = 49 ft². Add: 56 + 49 = 105 ft².

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 13 − 7 = 6 and 9 − 4 = 5. Whole rectangle 13 × 9 = 117, minus the missing corner 6 × 5 = 30: 117 − 30 = 87 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 11 × 8 = 88 ft². Triangle: its base is the 8 ft side and its height is 5 ft, so 12 × 8 × 5 = 12 × 40 = 20 ft². Add: 88 + 20 = 108 ft².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (gray dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 13 × 9 = 117 ft². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 × 24 = 12 ft². Subtract: 117 − 12 = 105 ft².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 5 = 60 m². The triangle's base is 18 − 12 = 6 m and its height is 5 m: 12 × 6 × 5 = 12 × 30 = 15 m². Add: 60 + 15 = 75 m².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle 12 × 7 = 84, minus the missing corner 5 × 4 = 20: 84 − 20 = 64 ft². Or: split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 49 + 15 = 64 ft².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 7 × 8 = 56 m². Each triangle: base 8 m, height 5 m, so 12 × 8 × 5 = 12 × 40 = 20 m². Total: 56 + 20 + 20 = 96 m².

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 12 − 5 = 7 and 10 − 4 = 6. Whole rectangle 12 × 10 = 120, minus the missing corner 7 × 6 = 42: 120 − 42 = 78 m².

items.q: Sofia tiles a patio shaped like a trapezoid. The parallel sides are 14 ft and 10 ft, and they are 8 ft apart. Tile costs $4.50 per square foot. How much does the tile cost?
items.e: Area: 12 × (14 + 10) × 8 = 12 × 24 × 8 = 96 ft². Cost: 96 × $4.50 = $432.

items.q: A kite is made of two triangles that share a 30 in rod down the middle. Each triangle is 10 in tall, measured from the rod. How much paper covers the kite?
items.e: Each triangle: base 30 in (the rod), height 10 in: 12 × 30 × 10 = 12 × 300 = 150 in². Two triangles: 2 × 150 = 300 in².

items.q: A park is a rectangle 80 m long and 60 m wide. It has a triangular pond with a base of 20 m and a height of 15 m. The rest of the park is grass. What is the area of the grass?
items.e: Park: 80 × 60 = 4,800 m². Pond: 12 × 20 × 15 = 12 × 300 = 150 m². Grass: 4,800 − 150 = 4,650 m².

items.q: A wooden sign is a rectangle 30 in long and 12 in tall with a triangle on one end, like an arrow. The triangle's base is the 12 in side, and it sticks out 8 in. What is the area of the sign?
items.e: Rectangle: 30 × 12 = 360 in². Triangle: 12 × 12 × 8 = 12 × 96 = 48 in². Total: 360 + 48 = 408 in².

items.q: Sam sews 12 triangle pennants for a banner. Each pennant has a base of 10 in and a height of 18 in. How much fabric do the pennants use in all?
items.e: One pennant: 12 × 10 × 18 = 12 × 180 = 90 in². Twelve pennants: 12 × 90 = 1,080 in².

items.q: Leo's sailboat has a sail shaped like a right triangle. The bottom edge is 9 ft and the mast side is 16 ft. What is the area of the sail?
items.e: The bottom edge and the mast meet at a right angle. A = 12 × 9 × 16 = 12 × 144 = 72 ft².

items.q: A flag is a rectangle 6 ft long and 4 ft tall. A blue triangle on the flag has a base of 4 ft (the short side) and a height of 3 ft. The rest of the flag is white. What is the area of the white part?
items.e: Flag: 6 × 4 = 24 ft². Triangle: 12 × 4 × 3 = 12 × 12 = 6 ft². White part: 24 − 6 = 18 ft².

items.q: Triangle A has a base of 10 cm and a height of 8 cm. Parallelogram B has a base of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. Which is true?
c: A is twice as large as B.
items.e: A: 12 × 10 × 8 = 12 × 80 = 40 cm². B: 5 × 8 = 40 cm². Same area. (Forgetting the 12 makes A look twice as large.)

items.q: A parking space is shaped like a parallelogram. It is 10 ft wide along the curb, and the painted slanted lines are 20 ft long. The distance straight across from the curb to the back of the space is 18 ft. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 10 × 18 = 180 ft². The 20 ft lines are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: Grace makes a triangle scarf. Its base is 1 12 yd and its height is 34 yd. How much fabric is in the scarf?
items.e: A = 12 × 1 12 × 34 = 12 × 1 18 = 916 yd².

items.q: A corner shelf is a right triangle. The two sides along the walls are each 34 ft long. What is the area of the shelf?
items.e: The two wall sides meet at a right angle. A = 12 × 34 × 34 = 12 × 916 = 932 ft².

items.q: A triangular sail has an area of 54 m². Its base is 9 m. How tall is the sail?
items.e: 12 × 9 × h = 54, so 9 × h = 108. h = 108 ÷ 9 = 12 m.

items.q: Ben paints the front wall of a shed. The wall is a rectangle 24 ft wide and 8 ft tall with a triangle on top that is 6 ft tall. How much area does he paint?
items.e: Rectangle: 24 × 8 = 192 ft². Triangle: 12 × 24 × 6 = 12 × 144 = 72 ft². Total: 192 + 72 = 264 ft².

items.q: A triangular sail has sides of 10 ft, 17 ft and 21 ft. The height to the 21 ft side is 8 ft. What is its area?
items.e: Use the 21 ft side as the base and the 8 ft height: A = 12 × 21 × 8 = 12 × 168 = 84 ft². The 10 ft and 17 ft sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A garden bed is a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are 3.5 m and 5.5 m, and the distance between them is 2 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × (3.5 + 5.5) × 2 = 12 × 9 × 2 = 9 m².

items.q: A triangular flower bed has a base of 12 m and a height of 7.5 m. How much ground does it cover?
items.e: A = 12 × 12 × 7.5 = 12 × 90 = 45 m².

items.q: An L-shaped lawn is a 40 ft by 30 ft rectangle with a 15 ft by 10 ft corner taken out for a patio. What is the area of the lawn?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 40 × 30 = 1,200 ft². Patio corner: 15 × 10 = 150 ft². Lawn: 1,200 − 150 = 1,050 ft².

items.q: A field shaped like a parallelogram has an area of 1,200 m². Its base is 40 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 40 × h = 1,200. h = 1,200 ÷ 40 = 30 m. (Halving is only for triangles and trapezoids.)

items.q: Each side panel of a skateboard ramp is a right triangle. The panel is 6 ft long on the ground and 1.5 ft tall. Both side panels get painted. How much area is painted?
items.e: One panel: 12 × 6 × 1.5 = 12 × 9 = 4.5 ft². Two panels: 2 × 4.5 = 9 ft².

items.q: Omar covers a stage shaped like a trapezoid with square tiles. The parallel sides are 20 ft and 12 ft, and they are 9 ft apart. Each tile covers 4 ft². How many tiles does he need?
items.e: Area: 12 × (20 + 12) × 9 = 12 × 32 × 9 = 144 ft². Tiles: 144 ÷ 4 = 36.
